hypotheses.title: Defaultable parameters cost O(K^2) per function: every default-value closure takes ALL preceding params, even when its default references none
hypotheses.issue: For a function with K defaultable parameters, the default-value closure for parameter i is always modelled as (paramTypes[:i]) -> paramTypes[i], whether or not its default expression uses any earlier parameter (most defaults are literals/constants). Stage 4 (setDefaultableParamFnSignatures) builds a function semtype with i params and allocates an i-length []model.Param per default; desugar (createDefaultClosures/createDefaultClosure) synthesizes i parameters per closure (newSimpleVariable, new VariableSymbol + scope AddSymbol, setSymbolType, associateFunctionSignature under the global signature store, a copied ast.BLangVariable, an unsized map entry); and every call site relying on defaults (hoistAndAddDefaultInvocations) passes hoistedArgs[:i] to each default call. That is K(K-1)/2 synthesized params per function and per defaulted call (~131k for K=512), which then also flows into BIR generation (i locals/args per closure/call). Only the earlier params actually referenced by the default expression need to be passed.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a .bal file with F functions, each having K defaultable int params.

usage: gen_defaults.py F K > out.bal
Total parameter count is F*K. Every default is a literal (references no earlier
parameter), yet each param-default closure is built with ALL preceding params,
so frontend work is O(F*K^2).
"""
import sys
F, K = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2])
out = []
for f in range(F):
    params = ", ".join(f"int p{i} = {i}" for i in range(K))
    body = " + ".join(f"p{i}" for i in range(K))
    out.append(f"function f{f}({params}) returns int {{\n    return {body};\n}}\n")
out.append("public function main() {\n    int s = 0;")
for f in range(F):
    out.append(f"    s += f{f}();")
out.append("    _ = s;\n}")
print("\n".join(out))
reproducer.command: python3 gen_defaults.py 8 512 > defaults_8x512.bal && /usr/bin/time -f '%e s %M KB' bal run defaults_8x512.bal   (compare shapes 64x64/32x128/16x256/8x512 with equal total params; stage times via debug build: bal-debug run --trace=t.json defaults_8x512.bal). Benchmark: ./bin/benchmark --mode time|memory --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> defaults_8x512.bal

hypotheses.fix_approach: Added DefaultableParam.ReferencedParams []int (ascending indices of preceding params the default expression references). In stage 4, setDefaultableParamFnSignatures builds a param-symbol->index map once per function (only if it has defaults), walks each default expression once (paramRefCollector in semantics/internal/types/walks.go; maps narrowed symbols back via unnarrowedSymbol; for BLangInvocation reads RawSymbol only when it is a *model.SymbolRef since method calls still hold deferred symbols, which also catches calling a function-typed param), and builds the typed/untyped closure signatures from only those params. Desugar's createDefaultClosures builds closure params from ReferencedParams (map presized), and hoistAndAddDefaultInvocations passes hoistedArgs[j] for j in ReferencedParams. ReferencedParams is serialized in model/symbolpool so cross-module callers agree. Pitfalls: the lint-walks purity check rejects slices.Sort/Compact in walks.go (used sort.Ints + manual dedupe); 142 desugared/BIR goldens change (only dropped unused closure params/args and renumbered BIR temps); added corpus test default-param-ref-earlier-v.bal covering non-adjacent references, function-typed param calls, lambda captures, function types, methods, rest params and named args. Defaults that really reference all earlier params remain inherently quadratic.
